newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Islamic stand sought on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Islamic stand sought on human cloning.

text.p: The head of an Islamic organisation has called on Islamic experts to find a "religious-and-science-based Islamic perception" to give guidance on human cloning.

In a statement sent to Reuters on Monday by the Islamic group ISESCO, its director-general Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri said the ever-accelerating pace and acute competition among scientific researchers provided "evidence that science is treading an unsafe path and evolving towards immoral objectives".

Altwaijri, head of the Islamic Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (ISESCO), called on delegates to "hammer out such a perception as may be tolerated by Islamic fundamentals and compatible with positive medical research trends", the statement said.
ISESCO, a cultural and scientific branch of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference, is co-sponsoring a four-day Religious and Medical Symposium in Casablanca which ends on Tuesday.
Altwaijri said rapid scientific progress, while useful to humanity, also left room for great concerns and many scientific and political meetings had taken a firm stand towards human cloning.

He said the Casablanca symposium was not intended to work out a final "fatwa" -- religious ruling -- nor final scientific opinion but join those making their voices heard towards setting up regulations for scientific progress in genetic engineering.
